name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (spec-build-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, and the ledger row driven; test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, and repair held by the session) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.55.0 — independent dispositions (specs/20260901/09-disposer-gate.md): the loop no longer parks after the reviewer returns to gate independence on a stale session id. `spec/agents/disposer.md` is a new fresh-context `spec:disposer` agent (`model: inherit`, read-only), dispatched at every DISPOSITIONS step on both review entries with no memory of the build; it returns one grounded `fix`/`waive`/`reject` recommendation per reviewer survivor and per failing non-blocking leg row. `spec-review-driver.js` refuses `--mark dispositions` on a non-empty pool without a disposer return covering every finding exactly once with a non-blank reason, records `disposer: {file, iteration, overrides}` in `review-state.json`, and retires the CHECKPOINT state, its session-id stamp comparison, and `--skip-independence-check-because` (refused by name, ADR-0005). `verdict.js`'s `--checkpoint` enum becomes `disposer|empty|not-reached` (`cleared`/`stamp-appeared`/`overridden` refused) with a new `--checkpoint-overrides <N>`, now accepted on `--via direct` and `--via` absent as well as `--via loop`; every review row's `checkpoint: {outcome, overrides}` records how often the user overrode the disposer. `review.md`'s DISPOSITIONS rule dispatches the disposer, applies `fix` recommendations without asking, and asks the user only on `waive`/`reject`; `build.md`'s enforced CHECKPOINT bullet is replaced by a no-stop bullet — independence is the disposer, on the loop path and the direct path alike. 7.54.0 — corpus derivation and the kill-match input (specs/20260901/08-corpus-derivation-and-kill-match.md): the replay corpus gains a `## Derived classes` region grown from the escape ledger — `spec/scripts/lib/replay-corpus.js`'s `parseCorpus`/`CORPUS_BAR` (2) is the one parser for both `replay.js` and `fleet-reader.js`. `replay.js --apply`/`--record` now refuse a `--class` outside the corpus (exit 2, valid ids named, nothing committed/appended) and a new `--pick-class` mode selects the next class to replay (fewest measurement rows, derived classes breaking ties first), retiring replay.md's own `--stats`-reading selection prose. `fleet-reader.js --json` gains `escapes.corpusGaps` (classes at or past the bar with no corpus section) and `escapes.registry` (every effective class, corpus membership flagged); `/spec:escape` reads `escapes.registry` for its `class` field and warns on a corpus gap after appending. Reviewer returns now carry `file`/`line` (explicit null when absent) on every killed claim, enforced at the `reviewer-returned` mark, so `/spec:escape`'s `killedMatch` derivation compares by file first. `replay-corpus.md`'s first derived class, `prefix-collision-coverage-fail-open`, is authored from the escaped `ac-matrix.js` prefix-collision fix. 7.53.0 — escape class contract (specs/20260901/07-escape-class-contract.md): every escape row now carries either a validated defect class or an explicit `unclassedReason` (`no-fix-diff`|`deferred`); `spec/scripts/lib/escape-row.js` is the one validator and `spec/scripts/escape-row.js` the one writer (`--check`, `--append` duplicate-refusing, `--amend`), retiring escape.md's `printf` append. A historical row's class is repaired by an append-only `stage:"escape-class"` amendment keyed by the original's `ts`+`spec`+`file`; latest amendment wins. `fleet-reader.js` counts recurrences on the joined (row + amendment) class, lists rows still needing a class as `escapes.unclassedRows`, and flags unvalidated rows in the drift census. `/spec:escape` classifies registry-first (fleet `byClass` keys plus the corpus's classes, before inventing a new id) and gains a one-time fleet-wide `--backfill` mode; `/spec:doctor` reports the backfill as due; core.md's Incident Policy Materiality bullet now cites the joined count.
